what: MEASURED 2026-09-22 in a Claude Code on the web container (this session): `python3 -m pytest tests/ -q` aborts with '149 errors during collection' -- ModuleNotFoundError on pandas and siblings. pytest itself was ALSO absent until I ran `pip install pytest` by hand. The repo ships requirements.txt / requirements-dev.txt / requirements-test.txt and nothing in the session bootstrap installs any of them; .claude/hooks/ contains only vm_lane_guard.sh. [!] THE DEFECT IS NOT THE MISSING DEPS, IT IS THE ABSENCE OF A SIGNAL. A lane that runs a targeted `pytest tests/test_foo.py` and sees green has no way to learn that ~149 other files never collected -- 'the tests I ran passed' and 'the tests that matter passed' are indistinguishable from inside the container, which is the collapsed-state shape docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md names. This session hit it while validating a TIER-3 real-money roster diff: tests/test_account_side_filter.py showed 6 failures, and only because I checked out origin/main's config/accounts.yaml and re-ran the file did I establish the same 6 fail WITHOUT my change (missing pandas, pre-existing). A lane that did not think to baseline would have read them as its own regression, or -- the dangerous direction -- a lane whose change DID break something in the 149 uncollected files would have pushed on a green partial run. [!] I DID NOT DIAGNOSE THE CAUSE and am not asserting one: I did not check whether the deps are deliberately omitted (container size, install time) or simply never wired. That determination is the first thing the lane should make, because it decides which of the two clears_when branches applies. [!] SCOPE OF MY OBSERVATION, stated because it bounds the claim: one container, one date, one repo checkout. I did not test a second session. === UPDATE 2026-09-22, same session, after the gap ACTUALLY BIT THIS LANE. The filing above says 'I DID NOT DIAGNOSE THE CAUSE'. It has now been diagnosed, and the finding is SHARPER than first written. [!] IT IS NOT MERELY 'THE DEPS ARE NOT INSTALLED'. requirements-test.txt exists and documents the one-line fix, but INSTALLING IT IS NOT SUFFICIENT: after `pip install -r requirements-test.txt` the suite STILL reported 44 collection errors. Reaching zero additionally required ccxt, email_validator, fastapi and httpx -- fastapi IS listed in requirements-test.txt yet was absent, because pip hit 'Cannot uninstall PyJWT 2.7.0 / cryptography 41.0.7, RECORD file not found' (both debian-packaged in this image) and THAT ERROR SILENTLY ABORTED THE REST OF THE INSTALL LIST -- the swallow-your-own-failure shape the canonical rules name, occurring inside the very file meant to fix this. Both needed `pip install --ignore-installed`. MEASURED progression: 149 collection errors -> 48 after pandas/numpy -> 44 -> 35 -> 0 after ccxt+email_validator, ending at 17,991 tests collected with zero errors, which matches the CI population. So the suite IS runnable here once the REAL dep set is present. [!] AND IT IS NO LONGER HYPOTHETICAL. PR #12707 (this row's own R2 cut, four legs off real-money/prop rosters) was validated locally, everything runnable was green, it was pushed, and CI came back RED with 6 failures in tests/test_breakout_prop_wiring.py, tests/test_m15_eth_pullback_wiring.py and tests/test_stale_decision_routing.py -- every one a test that PINS THE EXACT ROSTERS THE DIFF CHANGED, and every one inside the uncollectible set. A TIER-3 REAL-MONEY ROSTER DIFF REACHED CI UNVALIDATED AGAINST THE TESTS WRITTEN TO GUARD IT. Here it cost one red cycle; the dangerous version is a lane reading 'green locally' as coverage and a reviewer believing it. [!] TWO FIXES, NOT EQUIVALENT: (a) make requirements-test.txt actually sufficient -- add the missing names and handle the debian-RECORD packages; (b) make a session UNABLE to mistake partial collection for coverage -- a SessionStart step running --collect-only and printing the error count, so the number is in front of a lane BEFORE it validates. (b) is the real fix, (a) is its precondition; (a) alone leaves the silent green intact for the next dep that drifts.
